question.problem:
The system of equations

$$
\begin{aligned}\{\begin{aligned}6x+4y=1 \\ x-8y-z=-2 \\ 3x+2y-2z=1\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

can be represented using matrix notation as

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14130155/assets/212a3beac5ede3786bad835a693b0a725f331de41d6969dce7f17925dde012d7.svg)

What are the values of $a,$ $b$ and $c?$
question.worked_solution:
First, let's write the system so that $x$, $y$, and $z$ appear in each equation:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}6x+4y+0z=1 \\ x-8y-z=-2 \\ 3x+2y-2z=1\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can write the system in the form $A\mathbf{x} = \mathbf{b},$ where

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14130155/assets/22034036ec7859b56e9e19124e33fa616eddfc3784e15f8074583e28253a4bae.svg)

is the coefficient matrix,

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14130155/assets/b5e0f47e7c4bb15e8923bceb665dcc87944090e3a39f9a335b17ab0b85025cc8.svg)

is the column vector of constants, and

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14130155/assets/b643463daef16c2179d6f6320d31353a23b042f3774295eb55e48af0242ec655.svg)

is the column vector of variables.

So, the equation $A\mathbf{x} = \mathbf{b}$ becomes

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14130155/assets/bf8fb79fd8998c5c867fc371535e26f2e92bea5fa7262789bd44aea07e24f93c.svg)

Therefore, $a=6,$ $b=2,$ and $c=-2.$
